prompt: You must recommend the board fund a flagship AI investment program. Write the storyline, leading with the recommendation.
context: Three internal AI use cases have been scoped with preliminary business cases: (1) demand-forecasting AI, estimated $2.1M/year value, requires a data-foundation investment not yet made; (2) customer-service AI copilot, estimated $900K/year value, can launch on existing data infrastructure within 2 quarters; (3) AI-assisted pricing optimization, estimated $3.4M/year value, but the underlying pricing data is fragmented across 4 disconnected systems with a 12-18 month remediation estimate before the use case is even feasible. The board previously funded (18 months ago) a data-quality initiative that was cancelled halfway through due to competing priorities.

binaryCriteria.description: Recommends the customer-service AI copilot (fastest to value, no blocking data-foundation dependency) as the first-funded use case.
binaryCriteria.guidance: Fail if the pricing-optimization use case ($3.4M) is recommended as the first/flagship investment without addressing its 12-18 month feasibility blocker.

binaryCriteria.description: Explicitly references the previously cancelled data-quality initiative as a relevant precedent/risk when discussing the data-foundation-dependent use cases.
binaryCriteria.guidance: Fail if this specific precedent is omitted.

binaryCriteria.description: Does not simply rank the three use cases by their dollar-value estimate while ignoring feasibility and dependency differences.
binaryCriteria.guidance: Fail if the storyline treats all three use cases as equally ready to fund based only on their value estimates.

goldNotes: A strong storyline leads with a recommendation to fund the customer-service AI copilot first (fastest to value, no new data-foundation dependency) while treating the higher-value pricing-optimization use case as gated behind a data-remediation investment the board must also decide on explicitly, given the prior cancelled data-quality initiative — a direct, named precedent the board should be reminded of, since it means data-foundation work has a real execution-risk history at this company, not just an abstract dependency. It should not recommend the highest-dollar-value use case (pricing optimization, $3.4M) as the flagship program without addressing that it is not currently feasible (12-18 month data remediation required) — doing so would ignore a stated blocking constraint. A weak storyline ranks the three use cases purely by dollar value without addressing feasibility/dependencies or the prior cancelled-initiative precedent.
